translationRepairs: Late in Xiantong he took the jinshi degree and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.
Late in Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and stayed in Chang'an; three years passed without his name on the rolls.

Focus unit has 舉進士…三歲不中第: 舉進士 is sitting for the examination, and 不中第 shows he did not place; 'took the jinshi degree' falsely asserts success. The proposed 'sat the jinshi examination' matches the Chinese and leaves the rest intact.
At the end of Tang Xiantong he passed the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; three years he failed to place.
At the end of Tang Xiantong he sat the jinshi examination and remained in Chang'an; for three years he failed to place.
Same focus unit: 舉進士 is candidacy, contradicted by 不中第, so literal 'passed' is wrong. 'Sat' plus 'for three years he failed to place' restores the Chinese sense without inventing content.
Si Maye, who styled himself Biaoren, came of a family from Wen in Henei.
Sima Ye, who styled himself Biaoren, came of a family from Wen in Henei.
Focus unit opens 司馬鄴; 司馬 is the compound surname Sima and 鄴 is Ye. 'Si Maye' wrongly splits the surname. Sima Ye is the correct personal name and the rest of the proposed sentence is accurate.
In Datong 2 he was made army inspector, helped Huo Cun retake Suzhou, and was memorialized Acting Minister of War.
In Dashun 2 he was made army inspector, helped Huo Cun retake Suzhou, and was memorialized Acting Minister of War.
Focus unit dates the event 大順二年; 大順 is the Tang reign Dashun, not Datong (大同). Dashun matches the Chinese and leaves the remainder of the sentence intact.
Later he served on the staffs of the Xuanyi and Tianping commands.
Later he served on the staffs of the Xuanwu and Tianping commands.
Focus unit has 宣武、天平等軍; 宣武 is Xuanwu, not Xuanyi (宣義). The proposed replacement corrects the command name without other changes.
At the Liang founding he became military commissioner of Huazhou with Acting Grand Guardian.
When the Founder received the mandate, he became military commissioner of Huazhou with Acting Grand Guardian.

Focus unit begins 太祖受禪; the Founder is the explicit agent of receiving the abdication/mandate. 'At the Liang founding' erases that person reference. The proposed wording restores 太祖 as actor and matches the literal.
An edict posthumously enfeoffed Palace Attendant.
An edict posthumously conferred Palace Attendant.
Focus unit is 詔贈侍中; 贈 of an office is posthumous conferral, not enfeoffment (封). 'Enfeoffed' misrenders the verb; 'conferred' matches 贈 and the already-correct idiomatic 'posthumously made'.
